Container-unit form clamp(0.75em, 1.6cqi + 0.4em, 2em) gives close numbers 12/14.08/18.23/28.8px WHEN wrapped in a declared container -- but with no container-type ancestor (the honest default: .page and every rail on this site deliberately refuse container-type per the padding-audits rails-as-containers decision) it reads the VIEWPORT instead of the card: a 250px card and a 1400px card at 3440 both land on the exact same 32px, and the identical 250px card gets 12.8px at 400 and 32px at 3440 -- padding tracking the screen, not the box wearing it.

decision.about: percent form or container-unit form for the new --pad-card token

options.say: clamp(0.5em, 2.6%, 2em) * var(--size) -- the padding-audits own proposal, no -1.1em deferral so a cards own width feeds it directly
clamp(0.75em, 1.6cqi + 0.4em, 2em) * var(--size) -- the briefs suggested cqi shape

decision.because: MEASURED: the percent form is viewport-independent and container-type-independent by construction (a padding percentage already resolves against the boxs own containing block), so it needs no container-type declared anywhere and behaves identically whether or not one is present -- matching the codebases already-made decision to keep .page and every rail OUT of container-type (padding-audit rails-as-containers). The cqi form needs every card ancestor to be a declared container to behave correctly, and when it is not -- the honest default here -- it silently reads the viewport: a 250px and a 1400px card at the same viewport can land on the identical padding number, and the identical card gets a different number at different viewports for no reason tied to its own size. Looked at both at 1920 and 3440 (look-1920.png, look-3440.png in the session scratchpad): near-identical at 740px width (19.23 vs 18.23px, both comfortably past the rejected 16px), but the no-container B row visibly does not track box width while the no-container A row is pixel-identical to the with-container one.
decision.alternative_cost: the percent forms floor (8px at 250px) sits exactly at the new lint checks 8px WARNING threshold -- not under it, so no false positive, but no margin either; a future narrower card could trip it and that is by design (8px really is too little padding for a bordered box holding text)

**`.card` exists — a padded `.surface`, by definition.** [/framework/styles/system/](/framework/styles/system/) shows it live: `.card` = `.surface`'s exact ground/hairline/radius plus its own `--pad-card` token, its own component-scale rhythm between children (`--gap`, not `.flow` — `.flow` measured visibly too loose for a card, confirmed by screenshot), a `--card-edge` status stripe, and a `.selected` state (an inset ink ring, not the accent — the accent-border look was tried on V3 and read as broken). Nothing was migrated; nothing on the live site wears `.card` yet.

**The token, chosen by a table and by looking.** Tested a percentage form (`clamp(0.5em, 2.6%, 2em)`) against a container-unit form on cards 250/480/740/1400px wide, at 400/1920/3440, with and without a `container-type` ancestor. Percentage: **8 / 12.5 / 19.2 / 32px**, identical with or without a container. Container-unit: close numbers *with* a container, but *without* one (the honest default — `.page` and every rail on this site deliberately isn't one) it reads the viewport instead of the card — a 250px and a 1400px card landed on the same 32px at 3440. Chose the percentage form.

**Zero-pixel proof.** Pixel-diffed five busy pages before/after, twice (two `framework.css` write rounds): three static pages stayed byte-identical across ~30 minutes; the two live-content pages (a page with a clock, the AI dashboard) matched their own baseline noise level from a same-content, no-CSS-change control pair.

**The rule**, merged into existing paragraphs (not appended) in `css`, `layout`, `new-css-class`, plus one line in `ui/readme.md`: **a page region takes `.pad`, a framed box takes `.card`, a control or a row keeps its own `em`.**

**Two WARNING lint checks landed in `Server/health.mjs`**: a framed box holding text under 8px padding (excludes buttons/fields after a first pass drowned in that expected noise), and a list of 8+ rows pitched over 40px. Proven true-positive/true-negative on a scratch page; run on five real pages — mostly harmless inline-code chips, five tabs, and two real-looking finds: `core/Page`'s own tree component at 49–69px row pitch, and a 41-row wall that reads more like a card grid than a tight list. **The mastermind's running watcher needs a restart to see these** — not restarted here, by rule.
